sheet-2-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 2 shows the north-east corner of Westville where Broadway leaves the town across Big Timber Creek by an iron draw bridge. Station Avenue and the multi-track Pennsylvania Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore Division) cross the top of the sheet. River Drive runs down from the railroad to meet Broadway and Crown Point Avenue at the left edge, where sheet 3 adjoins. Block 16, between River Drive, the railroad and Broadway, is mostly open, with storage sheds along River Drive and a filling station on Broadway. South of Broadway, block 19 between Edgewater Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue holds a concrete block auto garage for fifteen cars, filling stations and dwellings numbered 1833 to 1839. Block 18 east of Pennsylvania Avenue has a filling station, an auto repair shop, a boat shop with a gasoline engine and a bridge house beside the draw bridge. Timber Avenue curves along the creek bank, lined with small frame dwellings on narrow lots, and splits at block 22 into Timber Avenue and North Timber Avenue, which run down a narrow peninsula enclosed by the creek (blocks 20, 21, 22, 23). The borough line follows the middle of Big Timber Creek. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 58 degrees clockwise, so north points up and to the right. The south end of block 21 is drawn separately in the inset at the lower left (part 2).
notes: Broadway on this sheet is modern Crown Point Road (Broadway was rerouted; the bridge crossing is now Crown Point Road).
Pennsylvania Avenue is modern Thomas Lane.
Crown Point Avenue is modern Crown Point Road.
Iron draw bridge over Big Timber Creek on Broadway.
Concrete block auto garage, capacity 15 cars, at Broadway and Edgewater Avenue.

Map, 50 ft. North-east corner: Broadway (modern Crown Point Road) to the iron draw bridge over Big Timber Creek, River Drive, Station Av, Pennsylvania Av (modern Thomas Lane), Timber Av, N Timber Av. Two parts: part 1 main map (turned, north about 58 deg clockwise of up); part 2 inset at lower left: south end of block 21 on the Timber Av peninsula, same scale and rotation, placed by carried lot corners from part 1. Part 1 uses 1 detected junction, 2 hand-picked junctions and 3 parcel block corners; Edgewater/Timber and the River Drive rail crossing were 22-30 m off and left out.

sheet-2-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 2 is an inset in the lower left corner, enclosed by a heavy line, showing the south end of block 21 on the peninsula in Big Timber Creek, between Timber Avenue on the west and North Timber Avenue on the east. It continues block 21 from the bottom edge of part 1 at the same scale and orientation (the figure 2 on the middle lot line marks the join); the first strip of lots at its top is the strip cut off at the bottom of part 1. The two streets, each 20 feet wide, close in towards the tip of the peninsula and meet in a rounded end at the bottom. The block is divided down the middle into two rows of lots, numbered 44 to 56 on Timber Avenue and 81 to 93 on North Timber Avenue, with small one and two storey frame dwellings on about half of them and several vacant lots. Big Timber Creek is drawn on both sides, with the borough line along it. The inset is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 58 degrees clockwise, like part 1.
notes: Placed by carrying two lot corners from the bottom edge of part 1 (same scale and rotation); low confidence.
Modern Timber Avenue follows the loop of the old Timber and North Timber Avenues around the peninsula.

Map, 50 ft. North-east corner: Broadway (modern Crown Point Road) to the iron draw bridge over Big Timber Creek, River Drive, Station Av, Pennsylvania Av (modern Thomas Lane), Timber Av, N Timber Av. Two parts: part 1 main map (turned, north about 58 deg clockwise of up); part 2 inset at lower left: south end of block 21 on the Timber Av peninsula, same scale and rotation, placed by carried lot corners from part 1. Part 1 uses 1 detected junction, 2 hand-picked junctions and 3 parcel block corners; Edgewater/Timber and the River Drive rail crossing were 22-30 m off and left out.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 is the commercial centre of Westville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left, about 30 degrees anticlockwise of straight up. Broadway runs up the middle of the sheet and is lined with shops, garages, a motion picture house, the post office and a bank. At the top Broadway divides: Crown Point Avenue leaves it to the left, running up the sheet beside the Westville and Newbold Water Company's pumping station and water tower on its western side, and Silver Lake Avenue leaves it to the right, running down the right half of the sheet past rows of dwellings to Center Street at the foot. The Boro Hall and Fire Department building (with the Union Fire Company hall above) stands on the east side of Broadway just north of Center Street, opposite the foot of Pine Street, and the 1st National Bank and the Toppin Inn are drawn on the triangle between Broadway and Silver Lake Avenue. Poplar Avenue branches off Silver Lake Avenue to the right and Edgewater Avenue follows the south bank of Big Timber Creek in the upper right corner, with a row of small frame dwellings along the water and a lumber shed, a garage and a carpenter and storage building behind. A railroad of the West Jersey and Seashore Division and Station Avenue run down the extreme left edge. River Drive crosses the top. Most buildings are two-storey frame stores and dwellings; the blocks along Broadway are densely built, while the blocks along Silver Lake Avenue and Poplar Avenue have large open yards. Block numbers 17, 24, 25, 28, 41, 81 and 82 are printed, and neighbouring sheets 2, 4, 8, 9 and 10 are named at the margins.
notes: Silver Lake Avenue is modern Delsea Drive (NJ 47); Crown Point Avenue is modern Crown Point Road.
Pine, Center and Broadway are lettered without a suffix; modern names are Pine Street, Center Street and Broadway.
Edgewater Avenue is lettered twice: near its junction with Timber Avenue at the top and along the creek bank to the right.
The modern Crown Point Road and Station Avenue lines lie 20 to 40 m from the drawn ones and were left out of the control.
Drawn scale 50 ft to an inch (scale bar read on the sheet); fitted 8.03 px/ft.

Map, 50 ft. Downtown: Broadway, Pine, Woodbine, Center, Silver Lake Av (Delsea Drive), Poplar Av, Crown Point Av, Station Av, Edgewater Av, Stanley's Alley. 4 junctions (three on Broadway, Delsea/Poplar); Crown Point Road, Station Av and Edgewater/Timber left out (modern lines displaced 20-40 m). Low-medium confidence.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the northern edge of Westville between Big Timber Creek at the top and Highland Avenue at the foot, with the railroad corridor of the West Jersey and Seashore Division (Pennsylvania Railroad) running down the right side. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page, so that north points to the upper left, about 43 degrees anticlockwise of straight up. The top third is industrial. On the left the J. Howard Coombs lumber yard occupies the creek bank, with lumber sheds, a sash storage building of concrete block, an office and open lumber piles; to the right of it a spur curves down from the railroad past a cement storage shed and a machine shop to a large semi-fire-proof works, built in 1905, drawn in pink and buff, with a transformer house, and a dock on the creek. The main line and its yard tracks fan out along the right edge with a railroad tool house beside them. Below River Drive the sheet is residential: 3rd Avenue runs down the middle between two rows of blocks cut by Summit Avenue and Highland Avenue, and Station Avenue runs beside the railroad on the right. The houses are frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys, numbered in the 200s and 300s along Summit and Highland Avenues, and the Baptist Church and its parsonage stand on the east side of 3rd Avenue above Summit Avenue. The streets to the left of 3rd Avenue continue on sheet 5, those below on sheet 8. Water pipes of four and six inches and fire hydrants are marked along the streets. Block numbers 9, 10, 11, 13 and 14 are printed.
notes: Scale bar reads 50 ft to an inch; fitted 8.04 px/ft.
Modern Station Avenue and Gateway Boulevard do not follow the drawn Station Avenue beside the railroad, so no junction on it was used.
The railroad crossing of River Drive on the right is the only control away from 3rd Avenue.

Map, 50 ft. River Drive, Summit, Highland, 3rd Av, Station Av beside the railroad; Coombs lumber yard, Baptist church. 3 junctions on 3rd Av plus the River Drive rail crossing. Seam pass move of 3.8 m refused (worse at the shared junction).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers a residential district in the north of Westville, between River Drive along the south bank of Big Timber Creek at the top of the sheet and Woodbine Avenue at the bottom, and between 5th Avenue on the left edge and 4th Avenue, which runs down the right third of the sheet. Summit Avenue and Highland Avenue cross the sheet between them, so the part shows two full rows of long, narrow blocks with the eastern ends of the next blocks beyond 4th Avenue. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned on the page: the street grid runs square to the sheet edges while north points to the upper left, about 43 degrees anticlockwise of straight up. Almost every building is a frame dwelling of one or two storeys set back on its lot with a small rear outbuilding or auto garage; a few are of concrete block or brick veneer. House numbers in the 300 and 400 ranges run along Summit and Highland Avenues. The lots between Highland and Woodbine Avenues are mostly vacant, with only the first row of houses along Highland built up, and the land behind River Drive is laid out in deep lots with scattered houses. River Drive itself is drawn as a diagonal road along the creek bank, cutting the top row of blocks at an angle. Water pipe sizes and fire hydrants are marked along the avenues. There are no industrial works, churches or schools on this sheet; it shows the edge of a 1920s suburban subdivision with many lots still open.
notes: Street labels read on a gridded overview and the scale bar on a full-resolution crop; small lettering was not read in full.
Drawn scale 50 ft to an inch; fitted 8.10 px/ft.
Map, 50 ft. Pilot sheet. River Drive, Summit, Highland, Woodbine, 4th and 5th Avs; residential.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the northern residential part of Westville between River Drive, which follows the south bank of Big Timber Creek along the top, and Woodbine Avenue at the foot. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, so that north points to the upper left, about 43 degrees anticlockwise of straight up. The block grid is square to the sheet edges: 6th Avenue runs down the left side and 5th Avenue down the right, and Summit Avenue and Highland Avenue cross between them, giving two rows of long, narrow blocks. The top row is cut at a slant by River Drive, which is drawn as a diagonal road beside the creek with lot lines fanning out from it. Almost all buildings are frame dwellings of one to two and a half storeys with small outbuildings, numbered in the 500s along Summit and Highland Avenues and in the 500s along the north side of River Drive; one dwelling at the left end of the second block is drawn in pink as a tile building, and a fire alarm box stands at the corner of 6th Avenue and Summit Avenue. Between Summit and Highland Avenues many long lots are empty at their rear. Below Highland Avenue only the first row of houses on the east side is built, and a club house and a sewage pumping station stand in the lots near Woodbine Avenue. The curving south-west shore of Lake Martha cuts across the lower left, and the lower left corner is blank. Block numbers 2, 5 and 7 are printed, and neighbouring sheets 5 and 7 are named at the margins. Water pipes of four and six inches and fire hydrants are marked.
notes: Scale bar reads 50 ft to an inch; fitted 8.15 px/ft.
Street names are lettered as 6TH AV. and 5TH AV. and written here as 6th Avenue and 5th Avenue; they match the modern names.
Map, 50 ft. 5th and 6th Avs, River Drive, Summit, Highland, Woodbine; Lake Martha at the bottom left. 6 junctions.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the north-west corner of Westville, where the street grid meets the Delaware River. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page, so that north points to the upper left, about 43 degrees anticlockwise of straight up. Delaware View Avenue runs down the left side of the blocks beside the river bank, River Drive crosses the top as a wide road drawn at a slant along the south shore of Big Timber Creek, Summit Avenue and Highland Avenue cross the middle and foot of the sheet, and 6th Avenue runs along the right edge. Together they enclose two rows of long, mostly empty lots; the lots on the river side have only a few frame dwellings, and the better built-up part is along 6th Avenue and the first lots of River Drive and Summit Avenue, where dwellings are numbered in the 600s. One house near the top right is drawn in pink as a brick building with a frame attic. A sewage treatment plant stands on the creek bank above the top left corner and a wooden trolley bridge crosses the creek mouth near the upper left edge. The Delaware River takes up the whole left third of the sheet, drawn with its wavering shore, and the south shore of Big Timber Creek runs across the top; Lake Martha appears in the lower right corner. Block numbers 1, 4, 115, 116 and 117 are printed in the blank areas, and neighbouring sheet 6 is named at the right margin. Water pipes of four and six inches are marked along the streets.
notes: Scale bar reads 50 ft to an inch; fitted 8.14 px/ft.

The Delaware View Avenue and River Drive junction was left out of the control because River Drive is drawn at a slant and wider than the modern road and it pulled the scale 1 percent from the other sheets.
Delaware View Avenue is lettered DELAWARE VIEW AV. along the river.

Map, 50 ft. Delaware View Av, River Drive, Summit, Highland, 6th Av; Delaware River. 5 junctions; Delaware View/River Drive excluded (River Drive drawn wide and slanted, px_per_ft 1 percent high with it).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the south-west part of Westville's built-up area around Lake Martha. The upper half is a residential district laid out on a grid turned about 40 degrees on the page: Highland Avenue crosses the top, Woodbine Avenue runs across the middle, and 3rd Avenue joins them on the left. West of 3rd Avenue are detached frame dwellings with a few blue-coloured concrete-block buildings and a laundry; east of it are St. Luke's Church (Episcopal), noted as heated by hot air and lit by electricity, and a Roman Catholic church (pink), followed by a long row of dwellings with outbuildings along the north side of Woodbine Avenue, a club house of concrete block and a fire alarm box at the corner of Crown Point Avenue. South of Woodbine Avenue a short block of dwellings stands between the dash-dot borough line and the lake shore. Crown Point Avenue runs from the Woodbine Avenue corner diagonally down the page, crossing the water on a concrete bridge; the borough line follows its west side. The lower left is occupied by Lake Martha, with its shoreline drawn in blue, and a compass rose. On the right, the passenger station of the railroad stands beside the tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore Division) at the edge of the sheet, and Station Avenue runs down the right side with a large area of narrow vacant lots between it and Crown Point Avenue. Lake Avenue is shown as not opened. Westville Public School No. 2, a stone building heated by steam, stands in the lower middle with a reinforced concrete foundation marked south of it. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn along the streets. The scale bar at lower left reads 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Highland Avenue, Woodbine Avenue and 3rd Avenue keep their names (OpenStreetMap: Highland Avenue, Woodbine Avenue, 3rd Avenue).
Crown Point Avenue is now Crown Point Road; the modern road is displaced from the drawn line (about 50 m near Woodbine Avenue), so it was not used as control.
Lake Avenue is marked 'not opened' and does not exist today.
Pine Street is read from the vertical lettering at the right edge, partly cut by the sheet margin (medium confidence).
The dash-dot line crossing Woodbine Avenue and following Crown Point Avenue is the borough line.
A concrete bridge carries Crown Point Avenue over an arm of Lake Martha.

Map, 50 ft. Highland, Woodbine, 3rd Avs, Crown Point Av, Station Av, Lake Av (not opened), Lake Martha; St Luke's, R.C. church, passenger station, Public School No. 2. 2 detected junctions and 6 parcel corners, all in the upper left; lower right extrapolated (mosaic preview shows Crown Point Av and Lake Av continuing into sheet 14). Modern Crown Point Road about 50 m off the drawn line, unused.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the centre of Westville between the railroad on the west and High Street on the east. Broadway runs down the middle of the sheet, about 66 ft wide, with its water mains drawn along it. On its east side the first block, between Center and New streets, is lined with small detached dwellings numbered 2 to 22, with the Westville M.P. Church (a spired frame church heated by hot air and lit by electricity) at its west end, and a two-storey dwelling at the corner where New Street bends north-east towards Silver Lake Avenue. South of New Street a row of dwellings faces New Street, and Public School No. 1 (stone, with a vapor system of heating, electric lights and fire extinguishers) stands at the east end beside High Street; further south a short row of dwellings fronts High Street. The large block numbered 44 between Broadway, Church Street and High Street is almost entirely vacant. St. Johns Lutheran church and a dwelling stand at the south-west corner of that block, and below Church Street another large vacant block numbered 45 has a few dwellings, a confectionery and ice cream factory and a cement-block outbuilding along its west side. At the upper left, Woodbine Avenue meets Broadway and Station Avenue runs down the left margin; a lumber, feed and fuel yard with sheds and a filling station occupies the block to its south. The west half of the sheet is filled by a tidewater pond with a compass rose on it, and the Pennsylvania Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore Division) runs along the left edge. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn in the streets. The sheet number 9 and the cartouche 'June 1926 Westville N.J.' sit in the top corners, the scale bar at bottom left.
notes: Church (the street between Broadway and High) is now Duncan Avenue; the control uses that name.
Center is now Center Street and New is now New Street; Silver Lake Avenue is now Delsea Drive.
Maple, at the bottom edge, is probably modern Birch Avenue (about 100 m south of Church on both Broadway and High); this is inferred from spacing and was not used as control.
Silver Lake Avenue is read from 'Silver' and 'Av.' on one line and 'Lake' beside it, partly hidden by the sheet number at the top right (medium confidence).
Woodbine Avenue and Center are drawn only 33 ft wide near Broadway.
The pond labelled Tidewater lies between Broadway and the railroad.
Map, 50 ft. Broadway, Center, New, Woodbine Av, Church (modern Duncan Avenue), High, Maple, Tidewater pond; M.P. church, Public School No. 1, St John's Lutheran church. 6 detected junctions.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows the eastern residential side of Westville between Silver Lake Avenue on the left and Big Timber Creek on the right, in a grid close to the page axes with north at the top. Four north-south streets, Silver Lake Avenue, Maple Avenue, Edgewater Avenue and, at the top, a diagonal continuation of Edgewater, are crossed by Poplar Avenue near the top, Center at the middle and West Avenue along the bottom. The blocks hold a continuous run of detached frame dwellings, mostly two or two-and-a-half storeys, with small outbuildings and a few stores, a club house, and several co-operative or storage sheds on the west side of the Center-to-West blocks (numbered 26, 27, 28, 48, 49 and 50). Between Edgewater Avenue and the creek the lots narrow into long strips running to the shore; there are a boat club and boat house, a pink-coloured building of two dwellings and small docks or outbuildings on the water side. Big Timber Creek is drawn in pale blue with its tidal edge, and a dash-dot borough line follows the creek. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are shown along Silver Lake Avenue, Poplar Avenue, Maple Avenue, Edgewater Avenue and West Avenue; fire alarm boxes stand at the corners of Center and Edgewater and of Maple and West. Street widths are lettered (60 ft for most, 40 ft on Edgewater and 20 ft at the north end of Edgewater). The adjoining sheet numbers (3, 9, 11 and 12) are printed around the edges and a margin note carries Center St. and New St. across to sheet 9. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the right, and the cartouche 'June 1926 Westville N.J.' sits at the top right.
notes: Silver Lake Avenue is now Delsea Drive (NJ 47).
Center is now Center Avenue on this sheet (OpenStreetMap: Center Avenue).
Center Street and New Street are lettered in the left margin as the streets continuing onto sheet 9; they are not drawn on this sheet.
Edgewater Avenue is drawn only 20 ft wide at its northern end, so its junction with Poplar Avenue was excluded from the control.
The dash-dot line in Big Timber Creek is the borough line.
The sheet is drawn with north to the top, unlike the sheets west of it which are turned.
Map, 50 ft, north up. Silver Lake Av (Delsea Drive), Poplar, Center, Maple, Edgewater, West Avs, Big Timber Creek. 8 detected junctions; Edgewater/Poplar excluded (Edgewater drawn 20 ft there).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers a thinly built area in the middle of Westville, east of High Street and west of Silver Lake Avenue, the main road running diagonally down the sheet from New Street at the top left to Almonessen Avenue at the bottom right. Sheet 10 adjoins at the top and sheet 9 on the left. At the top left a single block between High Street, New Street and Silver Lake Avenue is built up with frame dwellings and garages, numbered in the 200s. Below it most of the sheet is open land. Duncan Avenue, marked private, runs from High Street, where it continues Church on the west side, diagonally up to Silver Lake Avenue. Beneath it a large pond with an irregular shore fills the centre of the sheet and drains under Silver Lake Avenue towards Big Timber Creek through a culvert. South-west of the pond are the L. C. Duncan Farms greenhouses, a range of long glass houses with a boiler house and a packing shed, heated by hot water. West Avenue and Snyder Avenue leave Silver Lake Avenue towards the east. At the bottom left Maple begins at High Street with a row of narrow vacant lots, and Almonessen Avenue leaves Silver Lake Avenue at the bottom right beside a fire alarm box. Street widths of 40 and 50 feet are given at the junctions. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 33 degrees clockwise, so north points up and to the left.
notes: Silver Lake Avenue is modern Delsea Drive (NJ 47).
Almonessen Avenue is modern Almonesson Road.
Duncan Avenue is marked private on the sheet; modern Duncan Avenue follows it.
L. C. Duncan Farms greenhouses south-west of the pond.

Map, 50 ft. High, New St, Silver Lake Av (modern Delsea Drive), Duncan Av (private), West Av, Snyder Av, Almonessen Av (modern Almonesson Road); pond and L.C. Duncan Farms greenhouses. 7 detected junctions.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the south-eastern edge of the built-up area of Westville, between Silver Lake Avenue on the west and Big Timber Creek on the east, and from West Avenue at the top to Hunter Avenue at the bottom. The northern half is a regular grid of long blocks between West Avenue, Snyder Avenue, Silver Lake Avenue and Edgewater Avenue. It holds scattered detached dwellings and outbuildings, a bake shop at the corner of Silver Lake Avenue, and, in the middle of the upper block, the large concrete-block factory of H. Linsk and Co., Factory No. 5, manufacturing frocks, with steam heat and fire extinguishers. East of Edgewater Avenue narrow lots run down to the tidal edge of Big Timber Creek, lined with small dwellings and a boat house. A stream named Run crosses the sheet from the concrete bridge on Silver Lake Avenue to Big Timber Creek and separates the northern blocks from a large vacant tract numbered 53. In the south the street grid turns: Twedell Avenue runs diagonally up the page and Timber Creek Avenue runs down to Hunter Avenue, with Almonessen Avenue along the lower left, enclosing a block of mostly vacant lots numbered 54 with a few dwellings and a co-operative building. At the east end of that block, along the creek, stand a long storage building, the Structural Iron Work works (pink) and a few dwellings, with concrete walls marked at the shore. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and fire alarm boxes are shown in the streets. A compass rose and the scale bar sit in the lower right, and the cartouche 'June 1926 Westville N.J.' at the top right.
notes: Silver Lake Avenue is now Delsea Drive; Almonessen Avenue is now Almonesson Road.
Timber Creek Avenue is now the south part of Edgewater Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
The modern Delsea Drive and Almonesson Road junction lies about 8 m south of the drawn one, so it was excluded from the control.
The stream label reads only 'Run', no preceding name could be read.
Linsk frock factory: H. Linsk and Co., Factory No. 5, Mfg. Frocks.
The Westville West Avenue label is printed 'West' with the sheet number 10 beside it ('West 10 Av.'), the 10 being the adjoining sheet.

Map, 50 ft. Silver Lake Av, Snyder, Edgewater, West, Twedell, Hunter, Timber Creek Av (modern Edgewater), Almonessen Av; H. Linsk and Co. frock factory. 6 detected + 1 parcel corner; residuals 2-4 m on Edgewater (drawn grid not parallel). Almonesson Road/Delsea node excluded (8 m off).

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the south-eastern edge of Westville between Almonessen Avenue on the west and the shore of Big Timber Creek on the east. Sheet 12 adjoins at the top. Three parallel cross streets, Hunter Avenue at the top, Dewey Avenue in the middle and Stanley Avenue below, run between Almonessen Avenue and Timber Creek Avenue and enclose two fully built blocks, numbered 56 and 58, of small frame dwellings with outbuildings on narrow lots. Water pipe of 6 inches is shown dashed along the margins of the streets, with fire alarm boxes at the corners of Hunter and Dewey Avenues and hydrants marked DH near the east end. South of Stanley Avenue a single row of ten houses, numbered 2 to 20, stands on the lots, and the rest of the block, number 123, is vacant ground down to the bottom of the sheet, which is marked no exposure. East of Timber Creek Avenue a strip of long, narrow lots, blocks 57 and 59, runs down to the creek and carries a few dwellings, a club house of concrete block, a store, boat houses and a marine railway with concrete walls. Block 122 near the bottom right holds a vacant farm with a cluster of frame sheds. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 38 degrees clockwise, so north points up and to the right, as the compass at the left edge shows.
notes: Almonessen Avenue is modern Almonesson Road.
Timber Creek Avenue is modern Edgewater Avenue; its junctions with Hunter, Dewey and Stanley fit the drawn corners to under 1 m.
Hunter, Dewey and Stanley Avenues keep their names today.
Scale bar read as 50 feet to an inch.
Map, 50 ft. Hunter, Dewey, Stanley Avs, Almonessen Av (Almonesson Road), Timber Creek Av (Edgewater Avenue); rotation +38 deg. 6 detected junctions.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers a largely unbuilt subdivision in the south-west of Westville, between Crown Point Road on the left and Station Avenue beside the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks on the right, with Lake Martha in the top left corner. Park Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet and Hazel Avenue the lower part; Elm reaches the bottom left corner; Lake Avenue runs down the centre and is marked not opened, as is Station Avenue for part of its length. Blocks 37, 38 and 39 in the upper half are laid out as rows of narrow building lots with no buildings at all, some of them fanning out where the lot lines change direction. The built-up part is the strip along Hazel Avenue and the blocks between Hazel and Elm (block 35 and 36), where scattered frame dwellings, auto garages and sheds stand on the lots, with a concrete block manufacturing shed near Crown Point Road and one brick building near Elm. A railroad spur leaves the main line at the right edge and curves across the sheet towards the United States Government reservation west of Crown Point Road, crossing Park Avenue's blocks and Crown Point Road. The borough line runs along Crown Point Road. Water pipes are marked in Hazel Avenue and along Crown Point Road. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Lake Avenue and part of Station Avenue are marked not opened.
Railroad spur to the Government reservation crosses the sheet.
Lake Avenue does not exist today; Park Avenue survives only near Crown Point Road on a different line, and Station Avenue here is roughly modern Gateway Boulevard.
Street labels read on a gridded overview and full-resolution crops of the west side only.

Map, 50 ft. Crown Point Rd, Park Av, Hazel Av, Lake Av (not opened), Station Av, Elm; spur to Govt reservation; mostly vacant lots. Only Crown Point / Hazel survives as a junction (modern Park Avenue on another line, Lake Av gone): anchored on that point at 8.1 px/ft and north -43.5 deg. Carried points from sheets 16 and 17 were not usable (the shared corners lie off sheet 14 or are not drawn on it) and a parcel corner on Elm gave 7.66 px/ft, so it was left out. Low confidence; the mosaic preview shows Crown Point Rd, Lake Av, Hazel, Elm and the railroad continuing into sheets 8, 15, 16 and 17.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 lies on the south-western side of Westville, between the P.R.R. (W. J. & S. Division) railroad, and High Street. Sheet 14 adjoins on the left, sheet 9 at the top and sheet 18 at the bottom. Broadway runs down the sheet from top to bottom; on its west side a long strip of block 42 is divided into deep lots, with a row of frame dwellings and outbuildings numbered 334 to 342 near the top, a few more dwellings near the bottom numbered 536 and 538, and a large vacant tract in between. Along the left edge Station Avenue and the railroad appear as a bundle of parallel lines. East of Broadway four platted blocks lie between Maple, Walnut, Cedar and Oak, each marked not open, so these cross streets are laid out but not built. Block 84, between Maple and Walnut, carries the only buildings on that side: three dwellings, a fire alarm box, a row of sheds and a small works with a store, a tools shed and outbuildings. Blocks 64 and 65 further down are divided into long narrow lots and are entirely vacant. High Street forms the east edge, with a 6 inch water main in Broadway and fire alarm and hydrant marks at the street corners. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 31 degrees clockwise, so north points up and to the left.
notes: Maple, Walnut, Cedar and Oak are marked Not Open; the modern streets of those names run elsewhere, so they were not used as control.
Park Av., at the left edge, belongs to sheet 14.
Placed from one block corner carried from sheet 18 and five parcel block corners; the modern Walnut and Cedar are not on the old lines.
Scale bar read as 50 feet to an inch.

Map, 50 ft. Broadway, High, Station Av, Park Av; Maple, Walnut, Cedar, Oak all Not Open and not on the modern streets of those names. Placed from one corner carried from sheet 18 and five parcel block corners; low-medium confidence.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the south-western edge of Westville, in the angle between Crown Point Road on the left and Folsom Street at the right edge. Sheet 14 adjoins at the top left and sheet 17 on the right. Three cross streets, Elm, Olive and Chestnut, run across the sheet at the top, middle and lower part, and Cleveland runs down from Elm to Chestnut, so that four blocks, numbered 32, 33, 30 and 31, are enclosed between the streets. They are filled with frame dwellings and small outbuildings on narrow lots, some of the dwellings built of concrete block, with lot numbers 101 to 132 and 201 to 235 along the street fronts. Below Chestnut Street the lots of block 61 are drawn in outline with a few dwellings along the street, and the ground below them is blank with the legend no exposure. West of Crown Point Road, at the top left, stand a green house, a concrete block dwelling and store, and the Cement Block Manufacturing works, with a vacant tract, block 124, lower down. Four inch and six inch water pipe is shown dashed in the streets and fire alarm boxes stand at the corners of Elm and Crown Point Road and Olive and Cleveland. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 60 degrees clockwise, so north points up and to the left.
notes: Crown Point Road keeps its name today.
Olive is modern West Olive Street, Cleveland is modern Cleveland Avenue, and Elm, Chestnut and Folsom are modern Elm Street, Chestnut Street and Folsom Street.
Buildings west of Crown Point Road include a green house and the Cement Block Manufacturing works.
Scale bar read as 50 feet to an inch.
Map, 50 ft. Crown Point Rd, Elm, Olive (modern West Olive Street), Chestnut, Cleveland, Folsom. 9 detected junctions; Crown Point junctions carry 1.8-3.6 m.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the south-western corner of Westville where the town streets meet the Pennsylvania Railroad, West Jersey and Seashore division. Sheet 16 adjoins on the left along Folsom, sheet 14 at the top and sheet 18 at the bottom right. Across the top, Hazel Avenue and the lower end of block 35 show a row of narrow frame dwellings and outbuildings numbered 833 to 840, cut off on the right by the diagonal line of Station Avenue. The centre of the sheet is two blocks, 34 and 62, between Elm, Olive and Chestnut, bounded on the east by the angled line of Railroad Avenue. Block 34 contains the Victoria M. E. Church, a frame building heated by hot air and lighted by electricity, with dwellings numbered 63 to 96 beside it and a small concrete block building near the railroad end. Block 62 is mostly dwellings, one of them concrete block, numbered 1227 to 1235 and 933 to 939. South of Chestnut the lots of block 61 are laid out between the street and a diagonal line, and a tract numbered 83 lies east of Railroad Avenue with a spur track curving away from the main line. The railroad runs in a bundle of parallel lines from top to bottom at the right. Four inch water pipe is shown in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 60 degrees clockwise, so north points up and to the left.
notes: Olive is modern West Olive Street; Elm, Chestnut and Folsom are modern Elm Street, Chestnut Street and Folsom Street.
Station Avenue and Railroad Avenue are not matched to a modern street; modern Gateway Boulevard runs further east and was not used.
Olive Street, printed at the right edge beyond the railroad, continues on sheet 18.
Placed from the Folsom Street junctions and seven parcel block corners; the east side has one corner of control only.
Map, 50 ft. Hazel, Station Av, Railroad Av, Elm, Olive, Chestnut, Folsom; Victoria M.E. church. 3 detected junctions on Folsom plus 7 parcel block corners.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the southern end of Westville around South Westville Station, between the Pennsylvania Railroad, West Jersey and Seashore division, on the left and High Street on the right. Sheet 15 adjoins at the top. Broadway runs down the middle of the sheet. West of it are the railroad's passenger platform along the left edge, the South Westville Station, a small watch box, and, above Olive, the Independence Fire Company Number 2 station, a brick building with a hall on the second floor, with a fire alarm box at the corner. Large vacant tracts, numbers 42 and 63, fill the rest of the west side and carry only scattered dwellings and outbuildings along Broadway. East of Broadway, Olive, Ambler Street and Walnut cross the sheet from Broadway to High Street and enclose blocks 44, 45 and 109. The blocks nearest Olive and Ambler are the most built up, with frame and concrete block dwellings on narrow lots, a pair of blue concrete block dwellings on Ambler, and a storage building and sheds in block 44, which is cut by a diagonal line of unclear meaning. The upper row of lots below Oak, marked not open, is unbuilt. Olive on the west side of Broadway is offset from Olive on the east. Six inch water pipe runs in Broadway and the cross streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 31 degrees clockwise, so north points up and to the left.
notes: Olive is modern Olive Street west of Broadway and East Olive Street east of it; Ambler Street, Walnut Street, Broadway and High Street keep their names.
Oak is marked Not Open; the modern Oak Avenue is not on this line and was not used.
Ambler Street is drawn 20 feet wide; its junction with Broadway was hand-picked.
Scale bar read as 50 feet to an inch.
Map, 50 ft. Broadway, Olive, Ambler St (20 ft, hand-picked), Walnut, High, Oak (Not Open); South Westville station, Independence Fire Co. No. 2. 6 detected, 1 hand-picked.
